Consult Summary:
- Traveler with seven days of fever, night sweats, myalgias, nausea, and fatigue after returning from Vietnam; plan includes malaria testing and inflammatory markers with urgent clinic evaluation or A&E if needed.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Several days of fever with hot and cold periods, night sweats, generalized muscle aches, nausea, reduced appetite, and fatigue.
- Onset, duration, progression: Symptoms began about seven days ago; fever persists with intermittent relief from OTC acetaminophen/NSAIDs; no clear pattern to fever.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors: Over-the-counter analgesics (ibuprofen and paracetamol) provide slight relief but symptoms continue.
- Associated symptoms: No cough, sore throat, ear pain, or diarrhoea; no dysuria; no rash; no neck stiffness; headaches related to screen use; back pain history noted but not acutely tied to current illness.
- Exposures: Recent travel to Vietnam (returned ~4 weeks ago). Took malaria prophylaxis (described as daily plus an additional agent; specific drugs not recalled). Engaged in trekking, cycling, and rural countryside activities.
- Past Medical History: Chronic back pain; under physiotherapist for posture and strengthening exercises.
- Medications: Seroxat (paroxetine); ibuprofen; paracetamol. Dose/route/frequency for OTC meds not documented; paroxetine dose not documented.
- Allergies: Pollen/allergic rhinitis.
- Social History: Female patient (Sarah Smith), nurse by occupation; non-smoker; moderate alcohol use; exercises moderately.
- Family History: Father died of heart attack in his sixties (age ~68).

Past Medical History:
- Chronic back pain; under physiotherapy for posture and musculoskeletal strength.

Medications:
- Seroxat (paroxetine) — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Ibuprofen (OTC) — dose/route/frequency not documented (taken at recommended daily dose).
- Paracetamol (acetaminophen) — dose/route/frequency not documented (taken at recommended daily dose).

Allergies:
- Pollen allergy (hay fever).

Social History:
- Occupation: Nurse.
- Smoking: Non-smoker.
- Alcohol: Moderate intake.
- Exercise: Moderate frequency.
- Vaccinations: Up to date (including Hepatitis B).

Family History:
- Father had myocardial infarction in his sixties (age around 68).

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not provided.
- Exam findings: Not documented.

Investigations:
- Planned/tests discussed:
  - Blood tests including thick and thin blood films to check for malaria.
  - Inflammatory markers (and other basic labs as indicated).
- Additional evaluation: Clinic-based examination in central London planned; alternative option for local A&E if convenient.
- Documentation: Provider will type up the rationale and tests in the consultation notes for presentation to reception.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Fever with systemic symptoms after travel; possible infectious etiologies including malaria; currently no focal source identified.
  - Plan:
    - Bring patient to clinic for examination today or arrange urgent evaluation (central London clinic or local A&E).
    - Order malaria testing with thick and thin blood films.
    - Order inflammatory markers and other indicated blood tests.
    - Document advised tests and plan in notes; patient to present to the recommended site.
    - Avoid return to work until evaluation is completed.
    - Admin to book appointment; patient to call the number provided after the consultation to book slots.

- Issue 2: Travel-related infection risk (malaria and other exotic infections) after return from Vietnam.
  - Plan:
    - Ensure malaria workup as above (thick/thin films).
    - Consider broader infectious workup based on exam findings; proceed per clinic evaluation.

- Issue 3: Chronic back pain; ongoing management not directly addressed in current visit.
  - Plan:
    - Continue current physiotherapy program focusing on posture and strengthening (as previously advised).

General Plan:
- Proceed with in-person examination and blood testing as described.
- Urgency of tests contingent on examination findings; patient advised to seek urgent evaluation if symptoms worsen.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements: No recorded vital signs or physical examination findings; no documented current objective measurements or imaging results.
- Internal conflicts: None identified in the transcript.
- Transcript quality: Conversation was generally coherent; some memory gaps (malaria prophylaxis specifics); minor repetition; overall adequate for planning urgent evaluation and testing.
